title: Why the Bay Can't Help
approved_by: operator Gate 2 ratification 2026-06-11 (4 calibration lines KEEP VERBATIM) + auto-post decision 2026-06-12
chunks: 1/ Every moderation call is a values call dressed up as a policy call. "Is this hate speech?" has no technical answer. The classifier outputs 0.83. What you do with 0.83 depends on what your platform thinks hate is.

2/ The taxonomy is a values call. The thresholds are values calls. The reviewer training is values calls. A trust and safety system is a values architecture with software underneath it, not the reverse.

3/ Bay Area trust and safety engineers do not lack skill. They lack a fixed point outside themselves. "What I personally feel is harmful" plus "what my peers also feel is harmful" is not a moral compass. It is a weather vane.

4/ I am writing this as a Christian, and I will not pretend otherwise. A moral compass requires a standard you did not invent and cannot revise to fit the moment. The Bay Area professional class does not have one.

5/ What they have is peer consensus and a confidence that their moral intuitions are the moral intuitions of any reasonable person. They are not. They are a worldview. Calling it neutral does not make it so.

6/ Your platform's users, from that worldview's logic, fall in the category of people who need to be corrected. The work you are paying them to do is, internally, the work of slowly correcting your users.

7/ The failure mode is not hostile. The Bay Area engineer shows up, is pleasant, and does the work. The taxonomy reflects Bay Area concerns. The thresholds are calibrated to Bay Area sensibilities. The drift is sincere.

8/ Six months in, you have a moderation system that reads, from the outside, like a slightly slower-moving version of every other major platform. You paid premium engineering rates to import the problem you started to solve.

9/ The alternative pool exists. It is small. It is not in San Francisco. Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox, Evangelical Christians. Military and law enforcement backgrounds. People with a fixed point outside personal preference.

10/ They share one thing: the capacity to recognize when a moderation call is hard. They can see both sides of a hard call as containing real people with real reasons. That is not common. It is the whole job.

11/ You cannot outsource your conscience to people who do not have one of their own. The consultancies will sell you a conscience anyway. You will pay to import the consensus you started the platform to escape.

12/ Full essay: https://eapentechnology.com/essays/why-the-bay-cant-help.html
